note: Hebrew minchah here is the regular tribute owed by a vassal (cf. v.4 "year by year"), not a voluntary gift as "presents" now suggests.
Hebrew matsevot are standing stone pillars and asherim are wooden cult objects of the goddess Asherah; the KJV's "groves" follows the Septuagint/Vulgate and misleads.
Hebrew asherah is a cult pole or image of the goddess Asherah, something "made," not a grove of trees.
Hebrew hashomronim are the (Israelite) inhabitants of Samaria who built the shrines; "Samaritans" evokes the later religious community, which this verse is not describing.
Hebrew miqqetsotam means "from the whole extent of them," i.e. from people at large rather than from Levites (as 1 Kgs 12:31); it does not mean "the lowest."
